title: What Should I Read First In The Bible
paragraphs: Where to Begin: A Guided Journey Into Scripture

Opening the Bible for the first time can feel overwhelming. With 66 books, countless stories, and deep theology, it’s natural to wonder, “Where should I start?” This Bible study provides a roadmap for newcomers and seasoned readers alike, helping you begin your journey with confidence and joy.
1. Start with the Gospels: Meeting Jesus

The heart of Scripture is the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. The Gospels—Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John—record the good news of who Jesus is and what He has accomplished for us. Beginning here grounds your understanding of the Christian faith in the person and work of Christ.
But these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name. -
John 20:31 NIV
Among the Gospels, John is often recommended for first-time readers. John emphasizes belief in Jesus as the Son of God and provides clear explanations of His purpose and identity.
2. Acts: The Birth of the Church

After meeting Jesus, many find it helpful to read the book of Acts. Acts records the spread of the gospel and the early Christian church’s growth, showing how the message of Jesus changed lives and communities.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth. -
Acts 1:8 NIV
3. The Epistles: Living Out the Faith

The letters (or epistles), especially those by Paul such as Romans and Ephesians, explain the meaning of Jesus’ work and offer practical guidance for Christian living. Romans, in particular, lays out the foundation of salvation by grace through faith.
For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works, so that no one can boast. -
Ephesians 2:8-9 NIV
4. Genesis and the Old Testament: Understanding the Big Story

Once you’ve seen the center—Jesus—go back to Genesis to see how God’s plan began. Genesis introduces God as Creator, humanity’s purpose, the problem of sin, and the beginnings of redemption. Exploring the Old Testament helps you appreciate the foundation on which the New Testament stands.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. -
Genesis 1:1 NIV
5. Psalms and Proverbs: Wisdom and Worship
For daily encouragement, many believers turn to Psalms for prayers and worship or Proverbs for practical wisdom. These books are both accessible and deeply nourishing.
Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path. -
Psalm 119:105 NIV
Tips for Reading the Bible
Pray before you read, asking God for understanding (Psalm 119:18 NIV).
Read with a purpose—look for what each passage teaches about God, Jesus, and salvation.
Use a readable translation such as the NIV, ESV, or CSB.
Consider reading with others or using a study guide for accountability and deeper insight.
Conclusion: Christ at the Center

No matter where you begin, remember that the whole Bible points to Jesus. The Scriptures “make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus” (2 Timothy 3:15 NIV). Start with Him, and let the Word of God shape your faith, hope, and love.
